examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}シャワーを{浴|あ}びた。
examples.english: I took a shower in the morning.

examples.japanese: シャワーのお{湯|ゆ}が{出|で}なくなった。
examples.english: The hot water stopped coming out of the shower.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}の{後|あと}はシャワーで{汗|あせ}を{流|なが}す。
examples.english: I wash off sweat in the shower after exercising.

notes:
シャワー (from English "shower") refers to both the shower fixture and the act of showering. In Japan, showers are often part of the bathing area ({浴室|よくしつ}) and used before soaking in the bathtub.

Common expressions:
- シャワーを{浴|あ}びる (take a shower)
- シャワーを{出|だ}す (turn on the shower)
- シャワーを{止|と}める (turn off the shower)
- シャワールーム (shower room)

Cultural note:
In Japanese bathing culture, the shower is typically used to wash the body before entering the {浴槽|よくそう} (bathtub) for soaking. Taking a quick "shower only" without a bath is more of a Western practice.
